There are lots of quality leather jackets in the shops that are not a name brand, but you need to know what you're looking for. Having said that there are considerably more poor quality jackets, and especially from name brands.

The leather: Pinch the leather between your thumb and index/middle fingers and roll it back and forth. Good leather will feel full and supple. If it's papery or hard then it's a poorer quality. Be sure to check several different spots because a jacket may be pieced together from several different hides. And even across a single hide the quality of the leather varies.

The construction:

1. Look at the seams, are they straight? Is there a lot of loose thread?

2. Lay the jacket on a table and see how flat the zipper is. The zipper on a really well made jacket will be flat. Usually it's a little wavy and that can be acceptable but if it's really wavy then it's a sign that it's not well made. Also look at the collar, make sure it's flat and not twisted.

3. Look at the cuffs, make sure they appear okay. Cuffs are hard to do well.

4. Check that the seams under the armpit line up and are finished neatly.

5. A rayon lining will wear out long before the leather does. But even quality jackets use it because it feels and looks good, but just so you know. And while you're at it make sure the lining has been neatly assembled and fits inside the jacket correctly.

Fit: A garment should feel comfortable AND it should look good and correct when it hangs on you. Put the jacket on and stand with you hands at your side in front of a mirror. Does it look good, or does it look like a sack or too tight? Are the sleeves too long/short? Does the shoulder seam match your shoulder? Extend both arms out in front of you palms facing each other, then bend your elbows so that you hands come to your chest. Is it too tight across the back? Do the sleeves bind your arms? You want to have a sufficient degree of freedom of movement. Similarly when you reach up or bend over to pick something up.

A quality leather garment is never cheap but it doesn't have to be killer expensive either. Generally so-called Leather Outlets are filled with poor quality goods, but there can be good stuff in there if you take your time to look.
